blocks.x: Idea 1: Base SI units for mechatronics

items.x: **Primary resource:** [MathsIsFun — Metric System of Measurement](https://www.mathsisfun.com/measure/metric-system.html) `[HTTP 200 — Verified by scripts/check_links.py]`
**What to read:** Read exact headings **`Metric System of Measurement`**, **`Meter`**, **`Kilogram`**, and **`Second`**.
**What to skip:** Skip **`Volume`** (liters) and **`Temperature`**.

**Key takeaway:** Every equation in physics and engineering assumes your numbers are expressed in **base SI units**: length in **meters (`m`)**, mass in **kilograms (`kg`)**, time in **seconds (`s`)**, Amperes (`A`), Volts (`V`), and Ohms (`Ω`).
**Primary resource:** [MathsIsFun — Metric Numbers (Kilo, Mega, Milli, Micro)](https://www.mathsisfun.com/metric-numbers.html) `[HTTP 200 — Verified by scripts/check_links.py]`
**What to read:** Read exact headings **`Metric Numbers`**, **`Common Big and Small Numbers`**, and **`Much Bigger and Smaller`**.
**What to skip:** Skip `tera`, `peta`, `exa`, and `femto`—in beginner mechatronics you primarily use `M`, `k`, `m`, and `µ`.

**Key takeaway:** A **metric prefix** is a multiplier placed in front of a unit: **mega (`M`)** $= \times 1{,}000{,}000$ ($10^6$), **kilo (`k`)** $= \times 1{,}000$ ($10^3$), **milli (`m`)** $= \div 1{,}000$ ($10^{-3}$), and **micro (`µ` or `u`)** $= \div 1{,}000{,}000$ ($10^{-6}$). Always convert prefixed numbers into base SI units *before* multiplying or dividing!

blocks.x: Mixing un-converted prefixes into an equation is the #1 calculation error in beginner robotics. Every formula you will meet in this roadmap—such as distance ($d = s \cdot t$) and kinetic energy ($E_k = \frac{1}{2} m s^2$)—strictly expects **un-prefixed base SI units**: meters (`m`), kilograms (`kg`), seconds (`s`), Amperes (`A`), Volts (`V`), and Ohms (`Ω`).

blocks.caption: Carry the units through the arithmetic and the equation checks itself.

blocks.x: For example, if a datasheet says a sensor is $15\text{ mm}$ (millimeters) wide or a pulse lasts $500\ \mu\text{s}$ (microseconds) and you forget to convert to meters or seconds before multiplying, your answer will be off by a factor of **$1{,}000\times$** or **$1{,}000{,}000\times$**! Follow a two-step habit on every problem:

items.x: **Convert all inputs to base SI units on the very first line of code** (so $15\text{ mA} \rightarrow 0.015\text{ A}$, $0.22\text{ k}\Omega \rightarrow 220\ \Omega$, and $250\text{ mm} \rightarrow 0.25\text{ m}$).

**Run the formula purely in base SI units**, and only convert back to `mA`, `ms`, or `mm` at the end if a display label needs it. In Python, scientific notation (`1e-3` for $10^{-3} = 0.001$ and `1e-6` for $10^{-6} = 0.000001$) makes prefix conversion clean and typo-proof:
**What is simulated and in which tool:** Runs 100% in Python (zero-install in [futurecoder.io](https://futurecoder.io/course/) `[verify in-app]` or locally via `python3`).
**What is real-hardware only:** Nothing in this lesson requires hardware.

def ma_to_amps(val_ma):
    return val_ma / 1000.0


def kohms_to_ohms(r_kohms):
    return r_kohms * 1000.0


def us_to_seconds(time_us):
    return time_us / 1000000.0


i_a = ma_to_amps(15.0)
r_ohm = kohms_to_ohms(0.22)
v_drop = i_a * r_ohm
t_sec = us_to_seconds(500.0)

assert round(i_a, 4) == 0.0150
assert round(r_ohm, 1) == 220.0
assert round(v_drop, 2) == 3.30
assert round(t_sec, 6) == 0.000500

print(f"15.0 mA = {i_a:.4f} A | 0.22 kOhm = {r_ohm:.1f} Ohm | V = {v_drop:.2f} V")
print(f"500.0 us = {t_sec:.6f} s")

items.x: **Confusing lowercase `m` (`milli` $= 10^{-3}$) with uppercase `M` (`mega` $= 10^6$):** Those two letters differ by a factor of **one billion ($10^9$)**! A $10\text{ mm}$ spacer is $0.01\text{ m}$, whereas $10\text{ M}\Omega$ is $10{,}000{,}000\ \Omega$.
**Multiplying instead of dividing for `milli` or `micro`:** Ask yourself: *"Is a millimeter smaller or larger than a meter?"* Smaller—so $250\text{ mm} = 0.25\text{ m}$, never $250{,}000\text{ m}$.
**Prefix conversion drill:** Convert each measurement into its base SI unit: (a) $250\text{ mm}$ to `m`, (b) $4.7\text{ k}\Omega$ to `Ω`, and (c) $100\ \mu\text{s}$ to `s`.
(a) $250\text{ mm} = 250 \div 1000 = \mathbf{0.25\text{ m}}$
(b) $4.7\text{ k}\Omega = 4.7 \times 1000 = \mathbf{4{,}700\ \Omega}$
**Multiplying converted units:** If $I = 0.5\text{ mA}$ and $R = 10\text{ k}\Omega$, what is the product $I \times R$ after converting both to base units (`A` and `Ω`)?

blocks.x: Convert first: $I = 0.5\text{ mA} = 0.0005\text{ A}$ and $R = 10\text{ k}\Omega = 10{,}000\ \Omega$. Then $0.0005 \times 10{,}000 = \mathbf{5.0\text{ V}}$.

items.x: **Time conversion:** How many milliseconds (`ms`) and how many microseconds (`µs`) are in $0.002\text{ s}$?
Always convert measurements into **base SI units** (`m`, `kg`, `s`, `A`, `V`, `Ω`) before plugging them into formulas.
